item.text:
No. In the current Search Toolkit, `KeywordRetriever` requires a `KeywordStoreIndex`, while the built-in Vespa backend implements `VectorStoreIndex`. Vespa is therefore supported for vector/semantic—and apparently hybrid—search, but not as the backend for `KeywordRetriever`. The `pydantic.ValidationError` is the expected type/interface validation failure, not a malformed keyword query.

Mistral’s documentation explicitly lists `KeywordRetriever` only “with a custom `KeywordStoreIndex`,” while Vespa is documented as a vector-store backend:

- [Search Toolkit components](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit#components)
- [Search index backends](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit/search-index)
- [Vespa backend](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit/search-index/vespa)

For keyword-only retrieval, use a custom `KeywordStoreIndex` (or another backend implementing that protocol). With Vespa, configure a keyword-only YQL/query profile and use the Vespa-compatible vector-store retrieval path instead; the docs state that Vespa query profiles can contain a YQL query for keyword-only search. ([Query profiles](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit/search-index/vespa/query-profiles))
